name: Letrozole (aromatase inhibitor endocrine therapy)
cyclesNote: continuous once-daily dosing for 5 years (adjuvant), extended to 7.5 to 10 years total may be considered for node-positive disease; continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity in metastatic disease

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Endocrine therapy REQUIRES hormone-receptor-positive disease (ER and/or PR positive). Letrozole is a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor and works only in a low-estrogen (postmenopausal) environment: it is used in postmenopausal patients, or in premenopausal patients ONLY with concurrent ovarian function suppression/ablation. HER2 is tested to guide added HER2-directed therapy and does not change the endocrine indication. Per DeVita 12th ed. (Chapter 16) and Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer, Principles of Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy (BINV-K).

histology: hormone-receptor-positive invasive breast carcinoma (histology-agnostic; includes invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC))
supportiveCare: Not myelosuppressive; no G-CSF or routine antiemetics required (oral endocrine therapy).

Ovarian suppression (OFS) is MANDATORY when used in premenopausal patients: GnRH agonist (e.g., goserelin 3.6 mg SC every 4 weeks) or surgical/radiation ablation. Per NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K 2 of 4 and 3 of 4; DeVita lines 186178 to 186180.

Bone health: aromatase inhibitors increase fracture risk and cause bone loss; monitor bone mineral density and consider a bisphosphonate or denosumab plus calcium/vitamin D (DeVita lines 30140 to 30145; NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K footnote q).
Arthralgia/myalgia occur in up to half of patients (DeVita line 30140).
monitoring: adherence to daily oral endocrine therapy (crucial to outcome)
bone mineral density (baseline and periodic) given fracture risk
in premenopausal patients on OFS: confirm ongoing postmenopausal-range estradiol; vaginal bleeding on an AI warrants urgent review
clearanceChecks: postmenopausal status confirmed (or OFS in place for premenopausal)

doseModificationRules.text: Options include switching to another aromatase inhibitor after a washout, or to tamoxifen; supportive measures include exercise, NSAIDs, or duloxetine (NCCN v6.2026 supportive-care discussion; DeVita lines 30138 to 30145). Physician decides.

drugs.name: Letrozole
drugs.notes: Letrozole 2.5 mg by mouth once daily is the single standard approved letrozole dose (not disease-specific); DeVita 12th ed states 2.5 mg daily at line 176120, with breast aromatase-inhibitor pharmacology at lines 30152 to 30159. Continuous (flat daily dosing; the days array marks once-daily administration within a nominal 1-day cycle). Nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor. Adjuvant duration 5 years, with extended aromatase inhibitor duration (7.5 to 10 years total) considered for node-positive disease (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K).

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: letrozole 2.5 mg PO once daily is letrozole's single standard approved dose (not disease-specific); DeVita 12th ed states 2.5 mg daily at line 176120 (a non-breast section) and covers breast aromatase-inhibitor pharmacology at lines 30152 to 30159; NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K lists letrozole as a category-1 aromatase-inhibitor option
